summary: Initial discovery focused on Dedicated capacity needs: isolation, reserved GPUs, burst/overage strategy, autoscaling expectations, and security/compliance concerns. Customer wants predictable latency for low-latency chat use-case, strong data isolation (no shared tenancy), KMS integration, and the ability to burst to hosted pool for peak end-of-month load. Next steps: pricing matrix, benchmark session, share traffic traces, security review.
topics: Burst strategy and fallbacks to hosted
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Asha Patel (RidgeBank Head of MLOps), Tom Reynolds (RidgeBank VP Eng), Megan Li (RidgeBank Security), Eric Gomez (RidgeBank Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick intros, and then Luca will run through the dedicated capacity questions. Can I get a quick go-around?
[00:10] Asha Patel: Sure, Asha here, I run our MLOps team, main use cases are customer support chat and a few doc summarization flows. We're evaluating dedicated because of isolation and predictability.
[00:22] Tom Reynolds: Tom, VP Eng. We're responsible for SLOs and cost. Interested in predictable throughput and how bursting works.
[00:31] Megan Li: Megan, security. Focused on data residency, KMS, audit logs, and vendor SOC2.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Great. Luca, over to you.
[00:44] Luca Morales: Thanks. Quick agenda: sizing, isolation model, burst/fallback, autoscale, and security. Starting with sizing - how many requests per second and p50/p99 latency targets?
[00:55] Asha Patel: Right now prod chat sees about 120 qps steady across daytime, spikes to about 900 qps during statement cycles, but those are short, like 15-30 minute windows. Latency target is p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for the user-facing chat. If we can't hit that, user experience degrades.
[01:20] Luca Morales: Understood. Are you currently using open models or third-party hosted APIs?
[01:25] Tom Reynolds: We're running a mix. Some internal Llama variants on prem for research, but production today calls OpenAI for generative responses. Cost is high and tenancy is a concern.
[01:36] Luca Morales: Ok, so Dedicated could give you reserved GPUs and isolation. For the latency numbers you mentioned, we'd typically recommend a cluster of 8-16 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on model variant, sequence length, and batching. We do a more accurate sizing after we see traffic traces and prompts.
[01:55] Eric Gomez: Quick question — is the Dedicated environment single-tenant with our VPC, or is it multi-tenant under the hood?
[02:02] Maya Chen: Good question. For Redwood Dedicated we provide tenant isolation at the infra layer — you get dedicated GPU hosts and a private networking boundary. For our Private offering we can go further with customer-managed control plane, but Dedicated is single-customer capacity in our tenancy with network isolation and per-customer encryption keys.
[02:20] Megan Li: And KMS? We need to use our KMS for key wrapping, if possible.
[02:25] Luca Morales: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. We can share the KMS integration doc. There are a couple of options - bring-your-own-key via our KMS proxy or direct HSM pairing for Private.
[02:40] Tom Reynolds: About bursting — you mentioned bursting to hosted. How does billing/overage work and what's the latency impact when bursting?
[02:50] Luca Morales: Burst behavior: you can configure a buffer of reserved capacity and a burst policy that allows overflow to Redwood Hosted. Billing for overflow is usage-based at hosted rates; we can include a blended overage cap in contracts. Latency will typically be a bit higher when routing to hosted capacity depending on region and model variant — we automatically route to the fastest compatible variant and have fallbacks. We can set hard caps so overflow is blocked if you prefer.
[03:18] Asha Patel: For our compliance we may need hard caps, but we also want some ability to handle short spikes without failing. Can we have policy-based routing that blocks any PII-handling calls from overflowing to hosted?
[03:29] Luca Morales: Yes that's possible. You can set routing policies by route or model to disallow overflow for regulated flows, while allowing non-sensitive flows to overflow. We also have prefix/KV cache options to reduce burst load.
[03:44] Priya Rao: Quick ops Q: what's the autoscale latency? If we have short spikes, how fast can dedicated auto-scale up?
[03:51] Luca Morales: Autoscaling speed depends on whether you have additional reserved nodes in an idle pool or if you spin up new hosts. For Dedicated with reserved pools we can have warm standby nodes for sub-minute scale, typical cold-start from zero to full is 5-12 minutes depending on instance type and region. Warm pools are our recommended pattern for tight SLOs.
[04:12] Eric Gomez: Would warm pool nodes be billed as reserved or on-demand?
[04:16] Maya Chen: Warm pools are part of committed capacity—priced as reserved, but you can tune how many warm nodes to keep idle. That gives predictable billing and fast scale.
[04:27] Tom Reynolds: What's the typical utilization target you recommend so we don't waste spend but still have headroom?
[04:33] Luca Morales: We usually recommend targeting 60-75% steady utilization with burst headroom for spikes. That balances cost and latency. The Optimize toolkit can provide recommendations based on your trace data.
[04:47] Asha Patel: On model management — can we pin specific model versions and do canary rollouts? We want to avoid regressions when updating models.
[04:55] Luca Morales: Absolutely. We support model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. There's also QA/eval hooks so you can run prompt sets and catch regressions.
[05:10] Megan Li: Security — aside from KMS and audit logs, we need evidence of SOC2 Type II and maybe ISO 27001. Do you have certs?
[05:19] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II; ISO is in progress and we can share portal access to our compliance docs. We'll attach the attestation docs in the follow-up.
[05:29] Megan Li: Great. Also need network egress controls and VPC peering.
[05:34] Luca Morales: Dedicated supports VPC peering and IP allowlists. For Private deployments we can do air-gapped setups but that is a larger engagement.
[05:43] Tom Reynolds: For benchmarking — we expect to run latency/throughput tests with our prompts. How do you instrument and measure?
[05:50] Luca Morales: We provide a benchmark harness and can run joint tests. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, tail latency, GPU utilization, token/sec and cost per 1k tokens. We'll need your sample prompts and a traffic trace to replay realistic loads.
[06:05] Asha Patel: We'll prepare traces. Also question on quantization — are quantized models supported on Dedicated? We've been looking at 4-bit to save costs.
[06:13] Luca Morales: Yes, we support quantized execution paths; kernel selection and compilation ensure correct behavior. For some models there are small quality trade-offs, we'll include quantization profiles in the sizing recommendations.
[06:26] Priya Rao: Monitoring and observability — do we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?
[06:33] Priya Rao: (continuing) We need integration with Prometheus and our tracing stack.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level billing, and tracing hooks. We can stream metrics to your Prometheus and support OTLP.
[06:45] Eric Gomez: Is there any maintenance downtime for Dedicated? What's the SLA?
[06:49] Luca Morales: Dedicated has an SLA depending on committed capacity, typically 99.9% for reserved clusters. We schedule maintenance windows and provide automatic failover policies. For critical setups we recommend a multi-region cluster and automatic fallback routing.
[07:05] Tom Reynolds: Cost question — how do you charge for idle warm nodes? If we keep warm pool to get sub-minute scale, that increases cost, right?
[07:12] Maya Chen: Correct — warm pool nodes are included in your committed capacity cost. We can model different warm pool sizes and show the delta in unit economics so you can pick the optimal trade-off.
[07:24] Asha Patel: About data residency — our bank has EU and US customers; some flows must stay in EU. Can we pin model serving and data to region?
[07:32] Luca Morales: Yes, policy-based routing by region is supported. You can have regional clusters and choose routing by customer geography. For extra control, Private deployments in customer region are possible.
[07:43] Megan Li: For legal/procurement — lead time for Dedicated is what? If we sign a reserved capacity contract, how long until provisioning?
[07:51] Maya Chen: Typical lead time is 4-6 weeks for Dedicated, depending on region and capacity. Private or on-prem takes longer — usually 8-12 weeks.
[07:59] Tom Reynolds: If we want a pilot, say 4 GPU nodes to start, can we do a short-term pilot?
[08:04] Maya Chen: Yes, we do pilot programs. We can start with a small reserved pool and convert to committed at renewal. Pilots have a short contract and benchmark targets.
[08:13] Asha Patel: One more — how do you handle model updates and regressions? If a new model version has worse quality, can we automatically rollback?
[08:21] Luca Morales: We have rollout policies with automatic rollback based on quality/regression alerts tied to your test prompts. You can also freeze a route to a specific model version.
[08:32] Priya Rao: Ops integration — who will be our SE contact for the benchmark?
[08:35] Maya Chen: Luca will lead that. I'll CC Priya and Asha once we schedule.
[08:41] Luca Morales: I'll propose two slots next week, and include a pre-benchmark checklist.
[08:46] Asha Patel: Sounds good. On overflow charging — can you give an example blended rate and cap? We need to model costs.
[08:54] Maya Chen: I'll include a pricing matrix with dedicated unit rates, warm pool pricing, and hosted overflow rates plus an example blended cap. We'll show a few scenarios for your spike patterns.
[09:03] Tom Reynolds: For benchmarking, we need to validate both latency and hallucination rates. Can Redwood run evals for hallucination detection?
[09:11] Luca Morales: Yes, we have quality monitoring and can run evals against your prompt sets to measure hallucination rates and regressions. We'll include that in the benchmark scope.
[09:22] Megan Li: Any special network requirements from our side for VPC peering?
[09:26] Eric Gomez: (chiming) We'll need to open some outbound ports, agree on IP space, and set up routes.
[09:33] Luca Morales: We'll provide a network runbook with exact firewall rules and preflight checks.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Quick recap — items: pricing matrix, benchmark scheduling, share traces/prompts, security docs. Anything else?
[09:47] Asha Patel: Please include recommended warm pool sizes based on our spikes and a cost vs latency graph.
[09:52] Maya Chen: Noted.
[09:55] Tom Reynolds: Also, can you include an example SLA for multi-region failover?
[09:59] Maya Chen: We'll add that.
[10:02] Megan Li: We'll review the SOC2 docs and come back with any gaps.
[10:06] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and materials by EOD tomorrow and the pricing matrix by next Friday.
[10:13] Asha Patel: Thanks all.
[10:15] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-heard words; speaker labels mostly accurate.
